html:
The Seychelles, uninhabited islands in the western Indian Ocean, were first settled in 1770, when French colonists from Mauritius landed with enslaved Africans on the island of Sainte Anne.

France had claimed them in 1756 and named them after the finance minister Moreau de Séchelles. Planters grew spices, cotton and food for the French base on Mauritius, using enslaved workers, who soon outnumbered the settlers.

Britain took the islands with Mauritius in 1810 and made them a separate colony in 1903. The mix of African, French and later Indian and Chinese settlers made the Creole people and language of the islands. The capital, Victoria, grew on Mahé, and the islands stayed remote until the airport opened in 1971.
sum: The Seychelles, uninhabited islands in the western Indian Ocean, were first settled in 1770, when French colonists from Mauritius landed with enslaved Africans on the island of Sainte Anne.
